rewrites.summary:
No documented sub-national signal exists for Apurímac: the country dossier lists this department among the regions where no region-specific trans law, ordinance, incident series or enforcement finding could be located, and all three attached sources are national in scope. The operative legal fact for a visitor is the national frame: a congressional package (bills 6506 and 8457, committee-approved February 2025) barring people from public sanitary facilities designated for the opposite sex at birth — with exceptions only for custody, medical attention, or accompanying an elderly person, a child under 12 or a person with disabilities — was approved by the plenary on 2 April 2025 and enacted as Law 32331 on 13 May 2025, so a trans traveler now faces a live national legal exposure when using public restrooms.

Practical safety: national data record 54 killings of TLGBI people between 2020 and 2023, with trans women most affected (30 of the homicide victims) and hate crimes rising (19 in 2023, up from 13 in 2022); no regional deviation is documented either way.
rewrites.tangentialFactors: The ban is legally contested: a university human-rights institute argues the measure violates the equal-treatment and non-discrimination principle of article 2(2) of the national constitution and article 1.1 of the American Convention on Human Rights, a regional human-rights treaty, and rests on a stigmatising stereotype that implicitly presents trans people as likely restroom harassers, while UN reporting shows trans people are more often victims than aggressors. An international human-rights group (May 2025) in turn warned the enacted law threatens free speech and trans rights — litigation and policy flux around the measure that colors, without changing, the operative exposure.
rewrites.localsOnly: Resident-facing data: national monitoring tallies 170 rights-violation cases of TLGBI people between 2020 and 2023, including state violence and incitement to discrimination, with 61 denuncias in 2020 alone, documenting the discrimination climate residents of this department share. No Apurímac-specific resident finding exists in the attached sources.
rewrites.outOfScopeNotes: No attached source contains an Apurímac-specific legal, enforcement or incident finding, and the dossier places this department among the regions with no documented sub-national signal.  Whether the national law is actually enforced at local level inside Apurímac is undocumented in the available material. The ban's 2026 status remains unverified from the available sources.

blindSourceSummaries: News reporting (20 Feb 2025): the national legislature's women-and-family committee unanimously approved a bill package merging two bills that would bar trans people from public restrooms not corresponding to their birth sex, with narrow exceptions (custody, medical attention, or accompanying an elderly person, a child under 12 or a person with disabilities), plus a ban on 'ambiguous' bathroom signage; an activist called the measure discriminatory and warned that restroom access would come to depend on staff's personal judgment, including identity-document checks. It contains no state/province-specific finding; for this record its value is the committee-stage history of the national rule.

A university human-rights analysis (15 Apr 2025) confirms that on 2 April 2025 the national legislature approved and exempted from a second vote a bill whose article 5 bars any person from entering or using a public sanitary service that does not correspond to their 'biological sex', save for narrow listed exceptions, and argues this directly violates equal-treatment and non-discrimination principles of the national constitution and of a regional human-rights convention, with the stated aim of preventing child sexual abuse resting on a stigmatising stereotype; it contains no state/province-specific finding, and its value is the analysis of the national framework governing the region.

A news report (22 Jul 2024) covering a national observatory's annual report records 54 murders of TLGBI people and 170 rights-violation cases over 2020-2023, with trans women more than half the homicide victims (30); killings rose to 19 in 2023 (12 trans women) from 13 in 2022, many committed with cruelty, and the 170 violation cases include official violence and incitement to discrimination (61 denuncias in 2020); it also recounts a February 2023 gang abduction of a trans sex worker killed with about 30 gunshots as part of an extortion scheme. It contains no state/province-specific finding; its value is the national hate-violence data this record relies on.
rewrites.notes: Split from merged summary per rule 6; national-framework sources retained as the operative frame a visitor stands under (rule 1). Enactment (Law 32331, 13 May 2025) carried from this record's freshness entries, which mark the committee-stage piece superseded.

blindSourceSummaries: News reporting (20 Feb 2025): the national legislature's women-and-family committee unanimously approved a bill package covering two bills that would bar entry to public sanitary facilities destined to the sex opposite to one's birth sex, with exceptions only for custody, medical care, or accompanying an adult, a child under 12 or a disabled person, and require unambiguous signage; as of publication it still awaited plenary backing. No state/province-specific finding appears; the national data frame the risk environment this record applies to the department.

rewrites.summary:
Adana has no province-specific law, ordinance or incident series in the audited record; a trans visitor here stands under the same national framework that binds every province. A leaked October 2025 draft omnibus justice package (the '11th Judicial Package') would enable criminal charges against LGBT people nationwide, and it contains no province-specific provisions; if adopted it would apply to this province unchanged.

Legal protections for a visitor: same-sex sexual activity has been legal since an Ottoman-era penal code (1858), and trans people have been able to change their legal gender since 1988 — the document-relevant pathway — but there is no comprehensive law prohibiting discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation or gender identity, and same-sex relationships receive no legal recognition, so marriage, civil unions and domestic partnerships are all unavailable and a partner has no spousal legal standing when travelling together. The LGBTI association Kaos GL reported that in 2025 anti-LGBTI hostility became institutionalised as a national policy line under a 'Year of the Family' campaign centered on the family, with senior officials' rhetoric and instructions to public institutions creating a climate encouraging rights violations — the practical-safety context a visitor encounters.
rewrites.tangentialFactors: Human Rights Watch, an international human-rights group, described the leaked draft as one of the most alarming rollbacks of rights in decades, and activists in the country's largest city held a press conference against it on 28 October 2025; as a leaked document its adoption status is the main adjacent flux.
rewrites.localsOnly: Resident-facing facts from the national overview: LGBTQ people are barred from serving openly in the military, and same-sex couples cannot adopt jointly or as individuals; no Adana-specific resident data appears in the attached sources.
rewrites.outOfScopeNotes: The attached province page yields no usable finding for this record. The draft package is a leaked document, so its adoption remains unverified. The surviving record carries no provincial breakdown, so neither a more protective nor a more hostile local regime can be established for this province; the documented national picture applies here unchanged.

Afyonkarahisar has no province-specific law, ordinance or incident series in the audited record; a trans visitor here stands under the same national framework that binds every province. A leaked October 2025 draft omnibus justice package (the '11th Judicial Package') would criminalise conduct deemed 'contrary to biological sex and general morality' and its so-called 'promotion' with up to three years in prison, participation in same-sex engagement or marriage ceremonies with up to four years, and would restrict gender-affirming care — surgery age raised from 18 to 25 and mandatory permanent infertility — with medical professionals fined or imprisoned up to seven years and trans patients up to three years for care outside the new limits; it contains no province-specific provisions, and as a leaked document it is not yet in force.

A 2026 recheck confirms the national crackdown pattern remains current, with no provincial reversal found.
